Section.title: Smart Production Solutions
Section.description: Full-stack developer for Smart Production Solutions
Section.Content:

The front-end is CanJS (markup templates + JS). Mainly, I extended and documented the integration / data-sync, and delivered a number of front-end increments.

Section.title: Andes
Section.Content:
Dec 2022 – Dec 2024

Andes provides software solutions for receiving and processing requests from private individuals as well as business and institutional clients. Among other things, their software deals with online forms, client resource management, accounting and geodata.

Keywords: vertically integrated, message based architecture, domain driven design (in a public works context).

Skills:
MVC / AngularJS / SQL / DevExpress
XML as a data resource.
Programming from a "unit test first" perspective / TDD

Among other things, during my time at Andes I tackled the following:

A: Graphically displaying workflows: these were generated too randomly and looked up via the browser address bar. I:
• rewrote the algorithm and display into a clean flowchart.
• added options for node scaling / sorting / wiggle.
• added a new back-end webpage for searching by id & owner

B: Components for request forms, new & updates added:
• HTML partials (MVC, AngularJS), WPF controller+controls.
• Back-end XML <-> in-memory object conversion.
• Implementing/updating input validation + I/O to SQL.
• Writing and testing SQL migrations where a change in data architecture was necessary.
• Writing & documenting unit tests

C: Inconsistent choices in text encoding created a risk of data corruption. I wrote back-end code that tested input for a bit value > 255. If so, it would then encode it to decimal unicode. This prevents SQL from changing things on a "best match basis". Proactively extended workflow validation.

D: clients wanted to be able to determine user permissions themselves.
• I created the necessary pages
• extended the API with lighter calls for performance reasons.

E: Creating and editing workflows required a lot of legacy knowledge, and old forms were often not updated with new rules. I:
• Extended existing validation to enforce edge cases
• Set up rules for extending this, so that editing workflows requires less domain knowledge.

F: Financial exports: these are pieces of C# code that generate financial charges based on request types, their duration, and the services and materials used. After being calculated and assembled in memory, they are exported to binary, often Excel or CSV. I regularly added and/or updated these financial exports.

G: Created and updated XML workflows / CSHTML pages.
H: Added a number of lighter API calls for better latency.

Section.title: BEE-Ideas
Section.Content:
Feb 2022 – Dec 2022

I took part in 2 projects for Bee-Ideas.

Project 1: embedded at Interconnect BV, Den Bosch.
In the first project we were tasked with creating an API and microservice that would let B2B clients register domain names online. I delivered the following:
• local 127* and 192* clients to test TCP/IP messaging.
• terminal GUI to test requests.
• encrypted SSL connection, in standard TCP/IP.
• an XML (de)serialization library that can dynamically order EPP commands.
• big endian int-prepended message I/O
• necessary CCRUDs (Check Create Read Update Delete) for setting up the test environment / registering domains.
• refactored into a multi-layer API, DTO-oriented, AutoMapper compatible.
By the end of this project, they had a working API that just needed a front-end to be added.

Project 2: remote for VisualContracts, Den Bosch.
In the second project, a client came with an idea and a dream, but no specifications. They wanted
to make "visual agreements" available online for their clients, by means of a website that would function as a website composer. We delivered an MVP / vertical slice.

I:
• Worked out the tech and feature wish list together with the client.
• Initial product/feature decomposition into a component diagram.
• Tier 0 data architecture, to get the ball rolling and align sprint goals.
• Determined the Angular component/service layout of the front-end.
• Implemented TypeScript in hard-coded HTML pages.
• Coded the API calls for creating and updating contract objects (typescript).
• Coded front-end persistence in local/session storage.
• Created and coded sorting algorithms to group clauses by contract type.
• Created JS code that handles instancing of complex objects from queries in forms.
• Wrote a manual the owners can use to run the site as a demo to attract investors.
• Documented the front-end code, to make onboarding easier for the next development group.
• Managed the merge to the unified develop branch, and ran pipelines.
• Gave 6 of the 8 sprint review presentations for the front-end.
